The early return carries the guard, so every other rejection still reaches setAudioFailed. The comment cites finding F120.

AbortError guard, sync throw path: reader.tsx lines 256 to 260 hold catch (error) { if (isAbortError(error)) return; setAudioFailed(true); clearStopTimer(); }. The sync throw and the promise rejection take the same branch, so neither path hides a real failure.

The only other stop timer, the pendingIndex hold, is a separate effect at lines 236 to 244. So a skipped clearStopTimer on an abort leaves no armed stop.

AbortError guard, shared helper: apps/storytime/lib/is-abort-error.ts lines 7 to 9 hold the same body that decodable.tsx held before this delta: typeof error === "object" && error !== null && (error as { name?: string }).name === "AbortError". git show 5024a9fd9 --stat prints one new lib file and two changed route files (exit 0), so one helper now serves both screens and no copy remains.

decodable.tsx keeps F120: decodable.tsx line 15 imports the helper, and lines 252, 262 and 380 call it inside playElement and playClip. The guard uses the same !isAbortError(error) shape as before, so an abort still shows no alert and no pressed state.

S4b condition: reader.tsx line 204 holds if (finished || (book.pages.length > 0 && pageIndex >= book.pages.length - 1)) markPartDone(doneKey);. A multi-page book writes nothing on page 1, because 1 >= 8 is false; the write runs when the reader reaches the last page or the end view.

One-page book: the same line writes on the first view of a one-page book, because 0 >= 0 is true. The S4b case asserts the exact record one_page_record={"2:1:book":true}, and it failed at the role base with one_page_record={}.
Idempotent write: markPartDone in lib/done.ts writes record[doneKey] = true, so a second write of the same key leaves the record unchanged. No double record is possible.
